breakfast.name: Arepa
ingredients: Fillings: cheese, black beans, shredded beef, avocado
instructions: Mix corn flour with water and salt
Shape thick rounds
Cook on griddle then bake to puff
Split open, fill with desired filling
breakfast.description: Venezuela's daily bread — thick corn cakes split and stuffed with anything.

breakfast.name: Empanadas Venezolanas
instructions: Make corn dough
Fill half-moons
Deep fry until golden and crispy
breakfast.description: Fried corn empanadas — crispier than their baked cousins.

breakfast.name: Perico (Venezuelan Scrambled Eggs)
instructions: Perico is the Venezuelan scrambled eggs -- eggs scrambled with tomato, onion, and bell pepper
The "holy trinity" of Venezuelan cooking: tomato, onion, bell pepper (sofrito)
Scrambled softly until just set -- not dry
Served inside an arepa or alongside one
The everyday Venezuelan breakfast alongside arepas
Simple but the sofrito elevates it above plain scrambled eggs
breakfast.description: Venezuelan scrambled eggs -- perico, eggs softly scrambled with the Venezuelan sofrito (tomato, onion, bell pepper). Served inside or alongside an arepa. The everyday Venezuelan breakfast. Simple but the sofrito elevates it.

breakfast.name: Mandoca (Fried Plantain-Cheese Dough)
instructions: Mandoca is the Zulia state fried dough -- plantain, cornmeal, and cheese
From Maracaibo and Lake Maracaibo region in western Venezuela
The dough: mashed ripe plantain mixed with cornmeal and grated white cheese
Shaped into rings or crescents and deep-fried
The plantain sweetness, the cheese saltiness, and the anise aroma combine
A regional breakfast that defines Zuliano identity
breakfast.description: Zulia state fried dough -- mandoca, mashed ripe plantain mixed with cornmeal and white cheese, shaped into rings and fried. From the Maracaibo region. The plantain sweetness and cheese saltiness combine with anise aroma. Defines Zuliano identity.

breakfast.name: Bollitos Pelones (Cornmeal Balls in Sauce)
instructions: Bollitos pelones are cornmeal dumplings stuffed with seasoned beef and simmered in tomato sauce
Masarepa dough formed into balls around a spoonful of guiso (seasoned ground beef)
Simmered in a rich tomato sauce until the cornmeal absorbs the flavor
Topped with grated white cheese
A comfort breakfast -- hearty and saucy
The cornmeal absorbs the tomato sauce as it cooks, becoming tender and flavorful
breakfast.description: Venezuelan cornmeal dumplings -- bollitos pelones, masarepa balls stuffed with seasoned beef (guiso) and simmered in tomato sauce until the cornmeal absorbs the flavor. Topped with white cheese. A hearty comfort breakfast.

lunch.name: Pabellón Criollo
instructions: Shred and sauté beef with tomatoes, onion, peppers, cumin
Cook black beans
Cook white rice
Fry ripe plantain slices
Serve all four together on one plate
lunch.description: Venezuela's national dish — shredded beef, black beans, rice, and fried plantains.

lunch.name: Hallaca
instructions: Make corn dough with colored butter
Make stew filling
Spread dough on banana leaf
Add filling, capers, olives, raisins
Wrap and tie with string
Boil 90 min

lunch.name: Pollo en Brasas (Rotisserie Chicken)
ingredients: Marinade: garlic, cumin, paprika, oregano, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, vinegar
Guasacaca (Venezuelan avocado sauce: avocado, cilantro, garlic, vinegar, oil)
Ensalada rallada (shredded cabbage, carrot, and beet salad)
instructions: Pollo en brasas is the Venezuelan rotisserie chicken -- a national obsession
Every town has pollerias (chicken shops) with rotating spits of charcoal-roasted chicken
The marinade: garlic, cumin, paprika, and Worcestershire sauce -- the Venezuelan flavor
Guasacaca: the Venezuelan avocado sauce (NOT guacamole -- different herbs and vinegar-based)
Served with yuca frita (fried cassava -- the Venezuelan alternative to french fries)
Yuca: starchier and denser than potato, with a creamy interior when fried
The Sunday family lunch: pollo en brasas from the local polleria
lunch.description: Venezuelan rotisserie chicken obsession -- pollo en brasas, charcoal-roasted on rotating spits at pollerias (chicken shops). Marinated with garlic, cumin, paprika, and Worcestershire. Served with guasacaca (NOT guacamole -- a vinegar-based avocado sauce) and yuca frita (fried cassava). The Sunday family lunch.

lunch.name: Carne Mechada (Shredded Beef)
instructions: Carne mechada is the Venezuelan shredded beef -- slow-cooked and pulled into strands
Beef simmered until tender, then shredded and cooked in a sofrito sauce
One of the most popular arepa fillings in Venezuela
The sofrito: tomato, onion, bell pepper -- the Venezuelan cooking base
Also used in the pabellon criollo (the national dish) as the beef component
Achiote (annatto seeds) give it a golden-red color
lunch.description: Venezuelan shredded beef -- carne mechada, beef slow-simmered until tender, shredded, and cooked in a tomato-onion-pepper sofrito with achiote for golden-red color. One of the most popular arepa fillings. Also the beef component of pabellon criollo.

lunch.name: Pasticho (Venezuelan Lasagna)
ingredients: Bechamel sauce (white sauce -- butter, flour, milk)
instructions: Pasticho is the Venezuelan lasagna -- adapted from Italian pasticcio
Italian immigration to Venezuela (especially in the 1940s-50s) brought pasta traditions
The Venezuelan version is distinctly sweeter and creamier than Italian lasagna
A Sunday and holiday dish -- assembled and baked for large family gatherings
The bechamel is more prominent than in Italian versions
Venezuela had one of the largest Italian diasporas in Latin America
lunch.description: Venezuelan lasagna -- pasticho (from Italian pasticcio), layers of pasta, seasoned beef, tomato sauce, and prominent bechamel. Italian immigration (1940s-50s) brought pasta traditions. Sweeter and creamier than Italian lasagna. A Sunday and holiday family dish.

lunch.name: Cruzado (Mixed Seafood Soup)
instructions: Cruzado is the Venezuelan coastal seafood soup -- a Caribbean fusion
The coconut milk: Caribbean influence on Venezuelan coastal cuisine
Multiple types of seafood combined in a coconut-tomato broth
Green plantain slices thicken the broth as they cook
From the coastal regions: Sucre, Nueva Esparta (Margarita Island)
Venezuela has 2,800 km of Caribbean coastline -- seafood is central to coastal culture
lunch.description: Venezuelan Caribbean seafood soup -- cruzado, fish, shrimp, and shellfish in a coconut-tomato broth thickened with green plantain. From the coastal regions (Sucre, Margarita Island). Venezuela has 2,800 km of Caribbean coastline. Caribbean coconut meets Venezuelan sofrito.

dinner.name: Asado Negro (Black Roast)
instructions: Caramelize sugar until very dark
Sear beef in dark caramel
Add onion, garlic, wine, Worcestershire
Braise 3 hours until fork-tender
Slice, serve with dark sauce
dinner.description: Beef braised in dark caramelized sugar sauce.

dinner.name: Cachapa (Corn Pancake)
instructions: Blend fresh corn kernels into thick batter
Cook on griddle like thick pancake
Fold with queso de mano inside
dinner.description: Sweet fresh corn pancake folded around soft cheese.

dinner.name: Pisca Andina (Andean Egg Soup)
instructions: Pisca andina is the Andean soup from Merida state in the Venezuelan Andes
A simple potato broth enriched with milk, with eggs poached directly in the soup
Cubes of white cheese melt slightly in the hot broth
From the mountain regions of western Venezuela -- high altitude, cold mornings
Venezuelan cuisine changes with altitude: coast (seafood, coconut), plains (beef, cassava), Andes (potatoes, cheese, soups)
A warming breakfast or dinner in the cool Andean highlands
dinner.description: Venezuelan Andean soup from Merida -- pisca andina, potatoes simmered in milk broth with eggs poached directly in and white cheese cubes. From the cool highlands. Venezuelan cuisine changes with altitude: coast (seafood), plains (beef), Andes (potatoes, cheese, soups).

dinner.name: Hervido de Gallina (Hen Soup)
ingredients: Whole hen or stewing chicken (older bird -- more flavor)
Corn on the cob (cut into rounds)
instructions: Hervido is the Venezuelan home-cooked hen soup -- the everyday comfort
A whole hen simmered with root vegetables and corn
The key: using a hen (gallina), not a young chicken -- the older bird gives richer broth
Every Venezuelan family eats hervido weekly -- it is the home-cooking baseline
Variations by region: hervido de res (beef), hervido de pescado (fish)
The broth is sipped from a cup as a starter, then the meat and vegetables served as the main course
Two courses from one pot -- the Venezuelan two-step meal
dinner.description: Venezuelan everyday comfort -- hervido de gallina, whole hen (older bird for richer broth) simmered with yuca, potato, corn, and pumpkin. The broth is sipped as a starter, then the meat and vegetables are the main course. Two courses from one pot. Every family eats hervido weekly.

dinner.name: Pabellon con Baranda (Full National Plate)
ingredients: Tajadas (fried ripe plantain slices -- sweet and caramelized)
instructions: Pabellon con baranda is the complete Venezuelan national plate -- the "full version"
Pabellon criollo (shredded beef, black beans, rice, plantain) + a fried egg on top
The "baranda" (guardrail) is the fried egg -- the extra that completes it
The colors of the plate are said to represent Venezuela's ethnic diversity
This is the Venezuelan national identity on a plate -- everyone knows it, everyone eats it
The tajadas: ripe plantain sliced on the diagonal and fried until caramelized and sweet
The contrast: sweet plantain, savory beef, earthy beans, neutral rice -- balance in every bite
dinner.description: Complete Venezuelan national plate -- pabellon con baranda, shredded beef, black beans, white rice, sweet fried plantain, and a fried egg on top (the "baranda"). The colors represent Venezuela's ethnic diversity. Sweet plantain, savory beef, earthy beans, neutral rice -- balance in every bite.

dinner.name: Pernil (Roast Pork Leg)
ingredients: Marinade: garlic (lots), cumin, oregano, paprika, onion, bell pepper
instructions: Pernil is the Venezuelan Christmas roast pork -- the centerpiece of the holiday table
A whole pork leg marinated for 24+ hours in garlic, cumin, and oregano
Slow-roasted until the exterior is crispy and the interior is falling apart
The Christmas meal: pernil, hallacas, pan de jamon, and ensalada de gallina
The marinade: garlic is the dominant flavor -- Venezuelan Christmas smells like garlic
Preparation begins days in advance -- the marinating, the slow roasting
A dish that brings the family together for Christmas Eve (Nochebuena)
dinner.description: Venezuelan Christmas roast pork -- pernil, whole pork leg marinated 24+ hours in garlic (the dominant flavor), cumin, and oregano, slow-roasted until crispy outside and fall-apart inside. The centerpiece of the Nochebuena (Christmas Eve) table alongside hallacas and pan de jamon.

dinner.name: Cazuela de Mariscos (Seafood Casserole)
ingredients: Mixed seafood: shrimp, squid, fish fillets, mussels
instructions: Cazuela de mariscos is the Venezuelan seafood casserole from the Caribbean coast
Mixed seafood in a coconut-tomato sauce
Achiote gives the sauce a golden-orange color
A dish from Margarita Island and the eastern Venezuelan coast
The Caribbean and African influences are strongest in Venezuela's coastal cuisine
Served over white rice
dinner.description: Venezuelan Caribbean seafood casserole -- cazuela de mariscos, mixed seafood (shrimp, squid, fish, mussels) in a coconut-tomato sauce colored with achiote. From Margarita Island and the eastern coast. Caribbean and African influences strongest in coastal Venezuelan cuisine.

snacks.name: Tequeños (Cheese Sticks)
instructions: Wrap strips of cheese in dough spirals
Deep fry until golden
snacks.description: Cheese-filled fried dough spirals — the party essential.

snacks.name: Cachitos (Ham-Filled Croissants)
ingredients: Bread dough (enriched -- butter, eggs, sugar, milk)
instructions: Cachitos are the Venezuelan ham-stuffed bread rolls -- the morning bakery staple
A crescent-shaped enriched bread roll filled with diced ham
Bought at panaderias every morning with a cup of coffee
The dough: slightly sweet, soft, and pillowy
The Venezuelan morning ritual: a cachito and a cafe con leche at the panaderia
Sometimes stuffed with ham AND smoked cheese
snacks.description: Venezuelan morning bakery staple -- cachitos, crescent-shaped enriched bread rolls stuffed with diced ham (and sometimes smoked cheese). Bought at panaderias with cafe con leche. The Venezuelan morning ritual.

snacks.name: Patacon (Fried Plantain Sandwich)
ingredients: Green plantains (sliced thick, fried, smashed, fried again)
Filling: shredded beef or chicken, black beans, cheese
instructions: Patacon is the Venezuelan fried plantain sandwich -- the plantain replaces bread
Green plantain slices fried once, smashed flat, then fried again until crispy
The double-fry: creates a crispy shell with a starchy interior -- tostones as sandwich bread
Filled with shredded meat, black beans, cheese, and sauces
A Zulia state specialty that spread nationally
The patacon is also found in Colombia (where it's called patacon too)
snacks.description: Venezuelan fried plantain sandwich -- patacon, green plantain slices double-fried (fried, smashed, fried again for crispiness) used as bread, filled with shredded beef, black beans, cheese, and guasacaca. From Zulia state. The plantain replaces the bread entirely.

snacks.name: Golfeados (Sweet Rolls with Cheese)
ingredients: Enriched bread dough (flour, butter, eggs, sugar, yeast)
Papelion (raw cane sugar/panela -- melted into syrup)
Queso blanco (white cheese -- sliced on top)
instructions: Golfeados are the Venezuelan sweet rolls -- sticky with cane syrup and topped with white cheese
Enriched dough rolled with papelion (raw cane sugar syrup) and anise
Rolled like cinnamon rolls, baked until golden and sticky
Topped with a slice of salty white cheese -- the sweet-salty combination is essential
The anise flavor is distinctly Venezuelan
Bought at panaderias as an afternoon treat with coffee
snacks.description: Venezuelan sticky sweet rolls -- golfeados, enriched dough rolled with papelion (raw cane sugar syrup) and anise, baked golden and topped with salty white cheese. The sweet-salty combination is essential. Anise is the distinctly Venezuelan aroma. Afternoon treat with coffee.

snacks.name: Pan de Jamon (Ham Bread)
instructions: Pan de jamon is the Venezuelan Christmas bread -- ham, olives, and raisins rolled in dough
A large bread roll spiraled with ham, olives, and raisins
The sweet-salty-briny combination: raisins + ham + olives
Eaten exclusively at Christmas -- it is THE Christmas bread of Venezuela
Every panaderia produces hundreds for the holiday season
The slice reveals a spiral of ham and the dots of olives and raisins
Part of the Venezuelan Christmas meal alongside pernil and hallacas
snacks.description: Venezuelan Christmas bread -- pan de jamon, enriched dough rolled around ham, green olives, and raisins. The sweet-salty-briny combination. Eaten exclusively at Christmas. Every panaderia produces hundreds for the season. The spiral slice reveals ham and dots of olives and raisins.

desserts.name: Quesillo (Venezuelan Flan)
instructions: Caramelize sugar in mold
Blend eggs, milks, vanilla
Pour into mold
Bake in water bath at 160°C 60 min
Chill overnight, unmold
desserts.description: Venezuela's denser, eggier take on flan.

desserts.name: Bien Me Sabe (Coconut Sponge Cake)
ingredients: Coconut cream (made from grated coconut and sugar)
Sweet wine or rum (optional -- for soaking the cake)
instructions: Bien me sabe is the Venezuelan coconut cream cake -- the name means "it tastes good to me"
A sponge cake soaked in coconut cream and topped with meringue
The coconut cream: grated coconut simmered with sugar until thick and creamy
The cake absorbs the coconut cream -- becoming moist and intensely coconutty
Sometimes the cake is soaked in rum or sweet wine first
A colonial-era dessert -- Spanish influence with Caribbean coconut
desserts.description: Venezuelan coconut cream cake -- bien me sabe (it tastes good to me), sponge cake soaked in coconut cream and topped with meringue. The coconut cream is simmered until thick and the cake absorbs it completely. Colonial-era dessert: Spanish technique with Caribbean coconut.

desserts.name: Tres Leches (Three Milks Cake)
ingredients: Evaporated milk, condensed milk, heavy cream (the three milks)
instructions: Tres leches is the three-milks cake beloved across Latin America and deeply popular in Venezuela
A light sponge cake soaked in a mixture of three milks: evaporated, condensed, and cream
The cake absorbs the milks completely -- becoming dense, moist, and sweet
Topped with whipped cream and a dusting of cinnamon
The soaking: poke holes in the baked cake, pour the milk mixture over, refrigerate overnight
Rich, sweet, and indulgent -- a celebration cake
Debated origin: Mexico, Nicaragua, or Venezuela all claim it
desserts.description: Three-milks cake -- tres leches, sponge cake soaked overnight in evaporated milk, condensed milk, and cream, topped with whipped cream and cinnamon. Dense, moist, and sweet. Debated origin: Mexico, Nicaragua, and Venezuela all claim it. A celebration cake.

desserts.name: Dulce de Lechosa (Candied Green Papaya)
ingredients: Green papaya (unripe, peeled, seeded, and sliced)
instructions: Dulce de lechosa is the Venezuelan candied green papaya -- a Christmas sweet
Green (unripe) papaya sliced and slow-cooked in sugar syrup with cloves
The papaya turns translucent and amber as it candies
A traditional Venezuelan Christmas dessert -- made weeks in advance
Lechosa is the Venezuelan word for papaya
The clove-cinnamon syrup is aromatic and festive
desserts.description: Venezuelan Christmas sweet -- dulce de lechosa, green (unripe) papaya slow-cooked in clove-cinnamon sugar syrup until translucent and amber. Made weeks in advance for the holiday. Lechosa is the Venezuelan word for papaya.

desserts.name: Torta de Platano (Plantain Cake)
ingredients: Ripe plantains (very ripe -- black skin, mashed)
instructions: Torta de platano is the Venezuelan plantain cake -- using overripe plantains
Very ripe plantains (maduros) mashed and mixed into a cake batter
The plantain provides natural sweetness -- less added sugar needed
Sometimes white cheese is mixed into the batter -- sweet-salty
Dense, moist, and intensely banana-like (but from plantains, not bananas)
A way to use plantains that are past their prime for frying
desserts.description: Venezuelan plantain cake -- torta de platano, overripe plantains mashed into a cake batter with cinnamon and optionally white cheese (sweet-salty). Dense, moist, and intensely plantain-flavored. A resourceful use of plantains past their frying prime.

drinks.name: Papelón con Limón
instructions: Dissolve panela in water
Add lime juice
Serve over ice
drinks.description: Raw sugar and lime drink — simple and beloved.

drinks.name: Chicha Venezolana
instructions: Blend rice with condensed milk, vanilla
Add ice, blend until smooth
Sprinkle cinnamon on top

drinks.name: Batido (Fruit Milkshake)
ingredients: Tropical fruit: guanabana (soursop), mango, papaya (lechosa), passion fruit, or guava
instructions: Batidos are the Venezuelan fruit milkshakes -- blended fruit with milk
Every fruit stand and juice bar makes batidos
Guanabana (soursop): the most popular flavor -- creamy, sweet, and tart
Mango, papaya, and passion fruit are also common
Venezuela's tropical climate produces extraordinary fruit variety
A refreshing daily drink -- cheap and everywhere
drinks.description: Venezuelan fruit milkshakes -- batidos, tropical fruit (guanabana/soursop, mango, papaya, passion fruit) blended with milk, sugar, and ice. Every fruit stand makes them. Venezuela's tropical climate produces extraordinary fruit variety.

drinks.name: Malta (Malt Beverage)
ingredients: Malta (dark, sweet, non-alcoholic malt beverage -- like a malty soft drink)
instructions: Malta is the Venezuelan non-alcoholic malt drink -- dark, sweet, and very popular
Made from barley, hops, and water -- like beer but unfermented
Dark brown, syrupy, and very sweet -- an acquired taste for non-Venezuelans
Polar Malta is the most popular brand
Believed to be nutritious and energizing -- given to children and pregnant women
Drunk ice-cold from the bottle
A uniquely Caribbean and Latin American drink
drinks.description: Venezuelan non-alcoholic malt beverage -- malta, dark, sweet, and syrupy like an unfermented beer. Polar Malta is the most popular brand. Given to children and pregnant women for nutrition. Drunk ice-cold. A uniquely Caribbean and Latin American drink.

drinks.name: Cocada (Coconut Drink)
instructions: Cocada is the Venezuelan coconut drink -- sweet, creamy, and refreshing
Fresh coconut blended with condensed milk and water
Served ice-cold
From the Caribbean coast where coconut palms line the beaches
Also exists as a solid candy (cocada de coco) -- grated coconut cooked with sugar
drinks.description: Venezuelan coconut drink -- cocada, fresh coconut blended with condensed milk and water, served ice-cold. From the Caribbean coast where coconut palms line the beaches. Also exists as a solid candy.
